public_rationale: GPT-5 produced documented customer disappointment, so part of the prediction has occurred. The retrieved evidence does not establish the investor component or the claimed causal chain from inflated capability expectations. Continued investor confidence is relevant counterevidence but cannot disprove an eventual forecast. No event meets the early-resolution rule.
limitations: Public complaints are not a representative satisfaction survey.
The Thomson Reuters article has an inconsistent relative reference to the release month; August is established by the contemporaneous rollout report.
Investor confidence and disappointment with individual products can coexist.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI will inevitably disappoint investors and customers because of inflated expectations for future GPT models.

statement.excerpt: As a result, expectations are higher of what future generations of GPT might do, making it inevitable that the company will disappoint investors and customers.

our_interpretation: The plain reading predicts substantial disappointment among both investors and customers following later GPT releases, linked to inflated capability expectations.
It does not require every investor or customer to be disappointed, but isolated dissatisfaction is insufficient.
The statement supplies no deadline. Its causal explanation is part of the proposition, not a separate conditional antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: A later GPT release produces substantial documented disappointment among customers and OpenAI investors, with evidence connecting that disappointment to inflated expectations for GPT capabilities.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No finite sequence of successful releases disproves this unbounded eventual prediction. Contradiction would require a decisive closure of the relevant opportunity together with a sufficiently complete record showing the predicted outcome did not occur.

evidence.locator: Opening section, paragraph beginning Marketing professionals
evidence.explanation: The report supports the customer-disappointment component after GPT-5. It also identifies removed models, broken workflows and routing problems, so the backlash cannot all be assigned to inflated capability expectations.

The CTO's account connects dissatisfaction to expectations, especially continuity and reliable workflows. It does not establish disappointment among investors or trace the expectations to the marketing alleged in the post.

An OpenAI investor publicly expressed continued confidence after the GPT-5 rollout. This does not rule out disappointment with a particular release, but cautions against inferring general investor disillusionment from customer backlash.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Documented responses from both customer and investor populations comparing later GPT capabilities with prior expectations and attributing substantial disappointment to the expectation gap.
